findings.title: Brick walls now show two misaligned brick patterns (procedural mortar grid drawn over the scanned bricks)
findings.where: src/render/world/materials/faceDetail.ts (the WR_FACE_BRICK block in FACE_DETAIL_FRAG: courseMm 75 and brickMm 215, mixed in with mortarMix 0.5)
findings.detail: The brick material already has a scanned brick texture. The new procedural courses are not tied to the scan's scale or phase, so a grey mortar grid now cuts through the middle of the scanned bricks on every brick wall seen up close. Reproduce: node tools/harness/play.mjs --root . --query "test=1&seed=3&autostart=1&quality=medium&archetype=kitchen-door" --script test-output/look4-review/facade2.mjs. Compare test-output/look4-review/facade-sill-crop.png (after: two overlapping brick grids) with facade-sill-crop-before.png (the same pose on the old surfacePatch.ts: clean scanned bricks). The spec asked for detail that reads at a distance, not a second, conflicting pattern near the camera. The procedural courses should either match the scan's layout or appear only where the scan has faded out.

findings.title: Plinth band and brick coursing are computed per primitive, so house facades get a dark plinth stripe and a coursing jump half way up the wall
findings.where: src/render/world/materials/faceDetail.ts: `float yb = vWrP.y + vWrSz.y;` (prim-local height) and the plinth `if (fh >= plinthMinHeightMm)` block
findings.detail: vWrP is the prim-local position (WR_LOCAL), so 'height above the foot' is measured from each primitive's own bottom. worldgen's facade (src/worldgen/catalog/interior/shell.ts facadeTemplate, through partition()) cuts the brick outer leaf into horizontal bands at every opening edge. On kitchen-door seed 3 the bands run 234 to 1050 mm and 1050 to 2250 mm, and each band taller than 600 mm gets its own 'damp plinth' at its bottom: a dark stripe at window-sill height (1050 to 1200 mm). The courses also restart at every band edge. Evidence: test-output/look4-review/facade-medium3/facade-sill.png, where the row luminance drops from about 60 to about 46 over the two courses just above the seam and the head joints jump there. The plinth needs a ground or object-base reference (world y against the terrain height or the object's lowest prim), and the courses need a shared world-y phase.

findings.title: Wooden stumps and logs get board staves and bright seam lines; the report says curved props get no face detail
findings.where: src/render/world/materials/surfacePatch.ts (`face = o.prim === 'rounded' && o.space === 'instance'`, WR_BOARDS for every 'wood*' id) together with src/render/world/primitives/primInstances.ts (cylinders and capsules are family 'rounded') and the WR_BOARDS block in faceDetail.ts
findings.detail: Cylinders are drawn with the 'rounded' family. The face logic splits their curved side into quadrants (|n.x|>0.7 or |n.z|>0.7) and lays 150 mm 'upright boards' with gaps and per-board tints on each quadrant. Any wood-sound or wood-decayed stump or log with a diameter of at least 250 mm and a length of at least 250 mm (FOREST.stump diameter 300 to 800, FOREST.log diameter 150 to 400) now reads as a barrel of planks. Where u switches from vWrP.z to vWrP.x at the 45 degree lines, a thin bright vertical line appears. Reproduce: woodland-edge seed 3 at medium with test-output/look4-review/log.mjs. Compare log-medium/log2-wood-sound-r400-900.png and log0-*-900.png with log-medium-before/ (same pose, old surfacePatch: a plain wood stump with no staves). The fog exemption also differs between the quadrant and diagonal regions. The report's 'Curved props (the playground dome, cylinders) get no face detail' is wrong. Natural wood (logs, stumps, canes) should be excluded by shape and object, not only by material.

findings.title: Minimap repaint is about 4 to 8 times as costly; the spec says to keep the cost as it is now
findings.where: src/ui/hud/minimap/model.ts paintPlate (per-class indicator fields, two-pass box blur, BLUR_PX 10); src/ui/hud/minimap/Minimap.tsx paint (structure and water fills, not measured)
findings.detail: Spec item 4: 'keep the cost of a repaint as it is now (say the number)'. The implementer reports 0.14 ms before and 1.1 ms after (3.3 ms at 352 px). My same-process comparison against the pre-task nearest-cell painter gives 1.05 to 1.40 ms against 0.27 ms, 3.8 to 5.3 times as slow. The new structure and water Canvas fills (up to 1200 rects, each with save/rotate/restore) are left out of the number, so the real repaint cost is not reported. The failing test src/ui/hud/minimap/model.look4.verify.test.ts 'repaint cost ... stays near the cost before the task' demonstrates it (limit: three times the old painter). The implementer flagged this for the integrator instead of meeting the criterion.

findings.title: The minimap border blur erases zones narrower than about two blocks
findings.where: src/ui/hud/minimap/model.ts paintPlate (blur radius round(10 px / 2.75 px per cell) = 4 cells, two box passes, cut at one half)
findings.detail: At the live resolution (64 cells of 16 mm over 176 px) a 4 x 4-cell zone (16 BU square) and a 4-cell-wide strip (16 BU, e.g. a path or verge) are blurred below the 0.5 cut and disappear completely: 0 pixels where the nearest-cell painter drew 121 pixels or 6.25 % of the plate. An 8-cell strip survives. Reproduce: the failing tests 'a one-block zone ... stays on the map' and 'a one-block-wide strip ... stays on the map' in src/ui/hud/minimap/model.look4.verify.test.ts. How often real worlds contain such thin zones was not measured. The implementer's before picture (minimap2/before-plate-nearest.png) shows one-cell steps, not the claimed 4-cell blocks, so thin features are possible.

findings.title: The CPU twin of the grass blade shader lacks the new near-ground floor
findings.where: src/render/world/vegetation/bladeShape.ts bladeVertex (`const keep = v.density * grassLodKeep(dCam)`) against BLADE_GLSL (qNear)
findings.detail: The file header requires BLADE_GLSL and bladeVertex to stay in sync. Only the GLSL got the NEAR_GROUND floor. At density 0.25, a blade of rank 0.5 that is 60 mm from the camera is drawn by the GPU, while the CPU twin reports fade 0. The twin is used by the 'no blade through the camera' tests and by dropletVisible, so those tests now check a different blade set from the one rendered at the low and test tiers. Shown by the failing test in src/render/world/vegetation/bladeShape.look4.verify.test.ts.

findings.title: Chamber food occupancy is rounded to whole loads
findings.where: src/ui/panels/inspect/rows.ts rowValue, NUMBER_ONLY includes 'food' and uses Math.round
findings.detail: occupancy.food is fractional: src/sim/nest/chambers/upkeep.ts adds it.c + it.p in loads. A store chamber holding 0.4 loads now reads 'Food 0 / 12'; before the task it read '... (0.4 / 12)'. Shown by the failing test 'chamber food occupancy is in loads ...' in src/ui/panels/inspect/rows.look4.verify.test.ts. 'food' should format with loads(), as the other load rows do.

findings.title: Site advice can contradict itself for the middle factor words
findings.where: src/game/flows/founding/siteAdvice.ts ADVICE (only bad words have their own entry; everything else falls back to `any`)
findings.detail: When the weakest factor carries a middle or good word that has no byWord entry, the `any` line is used. Fair ground whose weakest factor is cover 'Leaf-covered' gets 'Leaf-covered: look for a stone, a log or leaf litter overhead.', which sends the player to look for what the read-out says is already there. Shown by the failing test in src/game/flows/founding/siteAdvice.verify.test.ts. I did not prove that this combination occurs on a generated world; it is a direct consequence of the table.

findings.title: Acceptance 2 coverage gaps beyond those the implementer listed
findings.detail: Item 2 asks for structures to read 'at quality test, low, medium and high'. Only test and medium were pictured. The backdrop car detail has no picture. Plastic play equipment and garden furniture get no material-kind detail at all (faceKindOf returns null for plastic). Item 5 asked for 20 degree, 45 degree, stem and nest-shaft pictures; only the 20 degree slope and the stem exist. The new problems above (double brick, stump staves, plinth stripes) would have shown up in close pictures of the structures, which were never taken.

findings.title: The near-ground floor distance is fixed in millimetres for BU 4, not 30 BU
findings.where: src/render/world/decor/tuning.ts NEAR_GROUND.mm = 120, baked into the GLSL in bladeShape.ts and drapedShape.ts
findings.detail: Spec item 3 says 'within 30 BU'. The 120 mm constant is compiled into the shaders, and the uDcBu uniform is not used for it, so for a species with BU 7 or 9 the floor covers only 13 to 17 BU. Only Lasius (BU 4) is playable today, so there is no visible effect yet.
